text:
Pope Leo's popularity among Catholic Republicans has dropped (Image: Corbis via Getty Images)

Pope Leo XIV has suffered a significant decline in his approval rating among Republican Catholics following his public feud with Donald Trump, according to a new poll.

While around eight in 10 US Catholics view the American-born pontiff favorably, tensions between Leo and Trump have hurt the pope's popularity among Catholics on the right, a new Pew Research Center poll found. The poll was conducted from May 26 to June 1, in the wake of escalating tension between Leo and Trump.

The pair had clashed over Trump's Iran war and immigration crackdown. In April, Leo spoke out against the conflict in the Middle East, blaming it on leaders having a “delusion of omnipotence.”

Trump hit back with a scathing social media attack on Leo as he branded the pope "WEAK on Crime, and terrible for Foreign Policy.” While 72% of Republican Catholics still approve of the pope, that has plummeted from 84% last August, the poll found.

It marked a much more significant drop in approval rating than Leo has faced among Democrat Catholics. A total of 84% of Catholics on the left approve of the pope, down from 89% in August 2025.

The pope is still viewed favorably among most US Catholics (Image: Corbis via Getty Images)

The same survey found that Catholic Republicans are far more likely than Catholic Democrats to say that the pope has been too critical of Trump.

Among Catholic Democrats, 70% said Trump had been too critical of the pontiff, while just 3% said Leo had been too critical of the president. But among Republican Catholics, 39% said Pope Leo has been too critical of Trump, as opposed to 33 percent who said the President has criticized the pontiff too much.

Pope Leo's approval rating among all US Catholics is currently at 78%, similar to the share who had a favorable view of his predecessor, Pope Francis, during the last years of Francis’ pontificate.

It comes as Trump renewed his criticism of Leo month, just days before Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited the Vatican in an attempt to ease tensions.

In an interview with conservative commentator Hugh Hewitt, Trump claimed the first American-born pontiff is helping Iran and also making the world less safe with his comments about the importance of not treating immigrants with disrespect.

“The pope would rather talk about the fact that it’s OK for Iran to have a nuclear weapon,” Trump said in the interview. “And I don’t think that’s very good. I think he’s endangering a lot of Catholics and a lot of people.”

The pope, however, has not said Iran should obtain nuclear weapons. He’s called for more peace talks, and criticized war with Iran generally and Trump’s specific threats of mass civilian strikes. The pope also has emphasized that he’s reflecting biblical and church teachings, not speaking as a political rival to Trump.

Leo responded to the president's criticism by calling out Trump's misrepresentation of his views. Speaking to reporters, the pope said the Catholic Church “for years has spoken out against all nuclear weapons, so there is no doubt there.”

Trump posted an image depicting himself as Jesus shortly after lashing out at the pope (Image: @realDonaldTrump/Truth Social)

He also doubled down on his insistence that his call for peace and dialogue in the US-Israeli war in Iran is biblically inspired. "The mission of the church is to preach the Gospel, to preach peace. If someone wants to criticize me for announcing the Gospel, let him do it with the truth,” Leo said.

In April, when Trump lashed out on Leo on social media, the pontiff responded by saying that God doesn’t listen to the prayers of those who wage war. Later, Trump posted a social media image likening himself to Jesus Christ, which he then deleted after backlash.

He has refused to apologize to Leo and has sought to explain away the social media post by saying he thought the image was of him as a doctor.
